headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Dealing with Standing Water
articleBody:
When you're faced with standing water in your sink or tub, it's easy to panic and try just about anything to get it moving. But trust me, some DIY fixes can actually do more harm than good, turning a simple clog into a much bigger and more expensive problem. Here are some common mistakes we see people make and how you can avoid them, especially if you're in the Goodyear, Buckeye, or Peoria area.

First, don't pour harsh chemical drain cleaners down the drain. While they promise quick fixes, these corrosive liquids can damage your pipes, especially older ones, and they're really bad for the environment. Plus, they rarely fix the root cause of a stubborn clog. Second, avoid over-plunging aggressively. While plunging is often a good first step, too much force or improper technique can actually push the clog further down or even dislodge pipe connections, creating leaks. Third, don't ignore the problem. A slow drain or occasional standing water isn't going to fix itself; it's usually a sign of a developing clog that will only get worse. Fourth, don't try to snake the drain yourself without the right tools or experience. You could accidentally scratch or puncture your pipes, leading to a much more significant repair.

And finally, don't assume every standing water issue is the same. There are various reasons for clogs, from hair and grease to tree roots in main lines. Trying a one-size-fits-all solution might miss the real issue. Instead, when these common fixes don't work, it's best to reach out to experienced professionals like Alpha-Plumbing Services, LLC.
